profile.tagline: If you can imagine it, you can program it
summary: I study Systems Engineering at Universidad del Cauca in Popayán, Colombia, and work as a full stack developer. I am currently at EzLife, building government information systems with microservices in NestJS, Next.js and React.

Thanks for taking the time to explore my portfolio. I hope you enjoy it as much as I enjoyed building it. If you have questions, proposals or just want to say hi, write to me through [this form](#contact) or by email at [juan_cardenas@qualityac.co](mailto:juan_cardenas@qualityac.co)

about.heading: About me
body: My motto is simple: if you can imagine it, you can program it. I move between two worlds that overlap more than it seems: full stack software development, and embedded and aerospace systems. In one I work with Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Next.js and React; in the other, with C on STM32 microcontrollers, telemetry and Kalman filters.

I started Systems Engineering at Universidad del Cauca in 2021. Since then I have worked on migrating monolithic systems to microservices, on security and access control (RBAC), on automated testing with Jest and Playwright, and on building websites as a freelancer. The details are on my [experience](#experience) page.

Since February 2025 I have been vice president of the IEEE AESS Unicauca student chapter. There I have led the chapter's teams at the UNAM CanSat world competition and at ENMICE, and the organization of the NASA Space Apps Challenge hackathon. Those projects are on my [aerospace projects](#projects-aerospace) page.

about.heading: Information fusion
body: My research interest is information fusion applied to navigation, drones/UAVs and state estimation. The International Society of Information Fusion (ISIF) awarded me the FUSION scholarship twice: in 2025 for the bootcamp in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, and in 2026 for the bootcamp at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) in Trondheim, Norway.

experience.summary: Design and implementation of government information systems with state- and role-based workflows. I work with NestJS, gRPC, Next.js, React 19 and Docker.
highlights: Migration of monolithic systems to a NestJS microservice architecture, communicating over gRPC and HTTP behind an API Gateway.
Modernization of legacy web interfaces to Next.js and React 19, keeping their visual identity and connecting them to the new services.
State- and role-based workflows, legal deadlines in business days, official numbering and traceability of administrative acts.
Bulk management modules for official data: bulk uploads, inventories by territory, and automatic and manual assignment.
Detection and fixing of security and integrity flaws: identity spoofing, non-transactional operations, silent data loss between services, and file uploads.
Quality assurance with more than 300 unit tests in Jest and end-to-end tests with Playwright on full Docker environments.
Integration of parallel development branches and technical documentation: test reports, business decisions and deployment guides with data migrations.
Software development and the organization's website.

experience.summary: Project funded by the IEEE DSTEI initiative to build an agricultural monitoring drone.
highlights: Design of sensor fusion algorithms (LiDAR, infrared, accelerometer and GPS) for the drone's navigation subsystem.

projects.title: JACUSys
description: JACUSys is my portfolio and the site you are on right now. It is an adaptation of Henry Heffernan's open source portfolio (MIT license), which I customized with my own information, warmer lighting and its own identity.

Technically, the site has two parts: a 3D scene and this 2D operating system. The scene uses Three.js to render a desk modelled and baked in Blender. The computer screen is this React site, embedded through an iframe and transformed with the Three.js CSS3DRenderer to create the illusion that it lives inside the monitor.

projects.title: TULCAN-SAT
description: Open source 2U CubeSat with controlled descent and no propulsion. The electronics are based on STM32, with LoRa telemetry and a PID controller combined with an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF). As team lead, I took the project to 8th place in the world competition.

images.alt: The TULCAN-SAT team in uniform during the competition, showing the CanSat inside a tube labelled TULCAN-SAT

projects.title: AIR-SAT
description: CanSat-type system with an optimized EKF to monitor air quality and rocket exhaust pollutants at high altitude. It won 1st place in the Picosatellite – Payload category.
